subject.title: [Bug]: Agents should not be able to access or modify files outside their own working space.

question: Should OpenClaw change the default agent filesystem boundary so host file tools and related runtime surfaces are workspace-confined unless an operator explicitly opts into broader access?
rationale: The current behavior is documented and compatibility-sensitive, but the reported failure is a real security/data-boundary concern; automation should not choose the default security posture or migration policy by itself.

options.title: Define a secure default policy
options.body: Keep this issue open and have maintainers specify the default confinement, explicit escape hatches, upgrade/doctor behavior, and docs before landing one coordinated fix.

options.title: Keep host-wide access opt-in documented only
options.body: Maintain the current default and close only after maintainers explicitly decide the supported answer is sandbox or `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` configuration rather than a default change.

options.title: Land a narrow partial fix first
options.body: Review a focused PR such as relative traversal hardening, but keep this issue open until the broader default and exec/native-runtime boundary are settled.

recommendation.title: Define a secure default policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and have maintainers specify the default confinement, explicit escape hatches, upgrade/doctor behavior, and docs before landing one coordinated fix.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest history on `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` resolution and the current security/sandbox docs that define the product boundary.
